- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to peak forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 10–15 day moving average of prior 10–15 prices.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term volatility; add 1–2% downward bias if sentiment is mixed or trending downward.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥ 0.67) over 5+ days, model may overfit to recent highs; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid “overbought” bias.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.80) and price is rising.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overestimates; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to avoid false momentum bias.
